anya: quick results from the regional latency sweep for model v2-quant (int8) across kernels and regions — throwing this in here before I forget :chart_with_upwards_trend:
anya: bench command I used: `./bench --model v2-quant --kernel auto --batch 1 --seq 512 --region {us-east,us-west,eu-west} --runs 200`
anya: summary (p50 / p95 ms) — A100-default-kernel: us-east 18 / 55, us-west 22 / 78, eu-west 26 / 95
anya: H100-llm-kernel: us-east 12 / 42, us-west 15 / 48, eu-west 18 / 60
anya: note: these include network + edge hop times (we hit edge routers in us-west and eu-west)
michael: looks like eu-west is consistently worse, especially p95. did you pin kernels the same way across regions?
anya: yes, kernel selection policy = `auto` for the run above. I also tried forcing `llm-opt` kernel on A100 and H100 — it shaved p95 ~10-15% on H100 in us-west but not on A100
jia: did you try disabling prefix caching? caching can reduce p50 but increases variance for p95 depending on routing
anya: good call — I re-ran with `--cache=off` for H100-llm and saw p50 similar, but p95 in us-west jumped from 48 to 82ms -> suggests some edge path variability + cold-cache misses
michael: that implies our edge routing + egress bandwidth in us-west is contributing. can we split tests using private deployment in each region (to isolate network)?
anya: I ran a direct private node test in eu-west (no edge) yesterday: H100-llm p95 dropped from 60 -> 30ms. so yep, network/edge routing is the main factor for eu-west difference
jia: quantization notes: int8 improved cost ~2.2x and p50 by ~20% but p95 is sensitive to kernel choice. some kernels don't have fused attention for int8 which increases tail latency
anja: (typo) — meant anya :grimacing:
oliver: for capacity sizing: if p95 varies by region so much, we should provision by worst-case p95 for SLA. proposal: scale targets use eu-west p95 on H100 as baseline, then autoscale thresholds per-region for observed tail latency
michael: agree. also add a routing policy: prefer hosts in region w/lowest recent p95 for soft routing, fallback to cheaper region only if underutilized
anya: I'll draft a short runbook: include kernel pinning, quantization matrix, and a quick check to decide if traffic should be routed around the edge (private nodes) for sensitive customers
sre-bot: deploy-bot: perf-bench-suite v3 finished in 1765126600, artifacts: https://ci.redwood/internal/bench/v3
ja: can someone add the raw CSV to the bench artifacts (so we can plot latency CDFs)? plots would help show tail behavior vs kernel
anya: uploaded CSVs to the artifact link and added a tiny notebook that plots p50/p90/p95 per region and per-kernel. notebook highlights: kernel-llm on H100 has tightest tail; A100 needs kernel-llm+quant tuning; if routing through our edge in eu-west, add 10-40ms tail penalty
michael: perfect. next step: run one A/B with routing-policy change for a small % of traffic in staging and monitor p95 delta over 24h
anya: adding to my plate, will create the canary and ping channel when ready :thumbsup:
